newsitem.title: LEBANON: MOST BEIRUT LEADING STOCKS FALL IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: MOST BEIRUT LEADING STOCKS FALL IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Most leading shares continued slipping on Wednesday in light trade on the Beirut Stock Exchange and brokers said investors were in a wait-and-see mood.
Turnover fell sharply to 67,755 shares from 234,570 shares on Tuesday and value dropped to $736,020 from $1,584,697.
"Everybody is in a wait-and-see mood. They are waiting for a small sign to get back into the game," Deputy Manager Alain Balian of Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.76 percent to 153.01. The LISPI general index fell 0.53 percent to 89.12 and the BLOM general index fell 0.09 percent to 925.56.
Brokers say a consolidation period on the market might last until the end of the month, when banks are expected to issue mid-year results.
Of the eight listed companies, three shares fell, one rose and one was unchanged. Three listed industrial companies were not traded.
Bank of Beirut fell to $3.875 from $3.9375 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce dropped to $18.125 from $18.25. Banque Audi was unchanged at its record high of $23.125.
Solidere A rose to $10.5 from $10.375 and B fell to $10.5 from $10.75 on turnover of 34,505 shares from 30,341 a day earlier.
Total demand for both shares on the first fixing was 332,089 against a supply of 51,090. Dealers say mismatching on prices kept volume down.
There was no trade in any of the four listed industrial firms: Ciments Libanais, Eternit, Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
